title: Reflecting on a Mountain Sunrise After a Hard Year
script: Narrator: [tired] I hadn't planned this hike carefully. I simply needed to leave the city after a year that had drained nearly everything out of me.
Narrator: [honestly] My friend suggested watching the sunrise from a nearby peak, and even though I was exhausted, something in me agreed almost immediately.
Narrator: [reflective] We started climbing at three in the morning, using headlamps, stumbling occasionally over roots we couldn't see clearly in the dark.
Narrator: [thoughtful] For most of the climb, I complained internally about my aching legs, wondering why anyone would choose exhaustion voluntarily after an already difficult year.
Narrator: [with feeling] However, as we reached the ridge, the sky began shifting from black to a deep, uncertain blue, and my complaining quietly stopped.
Narrator: [amazed] Then, gradually, thin orange light spread along the horizon, touching the clouds below us, since we were actually standing above them at that altitude.
Narrator: [with feeling] I had never seen clouds from above like that, spread out like some enormous, slowly shifting ocean beneath our feet.
Narrator: [reflective] I thought about everything that had happened this year, the job I lost, the friendship that quietly ended, the constant tiredness I couldn't explain to anyone.
Narrator: [gently] Yet watching that light spread so patiently across the sky, none of it rushing, none of it forced, something in my chest finally loosened.
Narrator: [warmly] My friend didn't say much, which I appreciated, since some moments don't actually need conversation to feel complete or understood.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I realized that even though my year had felt like one long, dark climb, mornings like this one had been waiting quietly the entire time, regardless of whether I noticed them.

Narrator: [peacefully] Despite everything difficult I had carried up that mountain, I walked back down feeling lighter, not because my problems had vanished, but because I remembered something larger existed beyond them.
Narrator: [with a small smile] Sometimes healing doesn't arrive through answers. Sometimes it simply arrives through light, patiently spreading across a sky you almost didn't bother climbing to see.
